recentItems.title: It's not a loneliness epidemic—it's an intimacy crisis | Justin Garcia | TEDxKC
recentItems.description:
Evolutionary biologist Justin Garcia argues that we've misdiagnosed the modern "loneliness crisis." It's not a lack of connection — it's a lack of depth. Drawing on research from the Kinsey Institute, he explains why our threat-wired nervous systems are simulating closeness instead of risking real intimacy, and explores what it takes to go deep again.

Dr. Justin Garcia is an evolutionary biologist and international authority on the science of sex and relationships. Since 2019, he has served as the Executive Director of the world-renowned Kinsey Institute, where he is also a Senior Scientist. He holds an appointment as the Ruth N. Halls Professor in the College of Arts and Sciences at Indiana University and is a Founding Co-Director of Human Sexuality and Health at the IU School of Medicine. Dr. Garcia holds a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology and M.S. in biomedical anthropology from Binghamton University and an Executive Certificate in Public Leadership from Harvard Kennedy School. An award-winning researcher and educator, Dr. Garcia has consulted with a variety of industry partners, and he is currently the Chief Scientific Advisor to Match, where he provides expertise for the annual Singles in America study. His research has been featured widely in the media and focuses on people’s romantic and sexual lives throughout the life course, especially on integrative biopsychosocial models of variation in courtship, intimacy, and sexual behavior. He has co-authored over 100 academic articles and book chapters, and is co-author of Evolution and Human Sexual Behavior. His latest book, The Intimate Animal, explores the science behind why we live and die for love. https://kinseyinstitute.org/research/intimate-animal.html 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Unleashing Our Potential in a Chaotic World | Roland Mees | TEDxUniversityofGroningen
recentItems.description:
Amidst the chaos around us, my question is: What inner source do we need to make the world a better place? Growing from within, how can we realise a visible, positive impact?
 

My response: by staying true to the fire within us. When we keep working on realising our deepest commitments, we may be able to steer the course of events towards a world we want to leave for future generations.

 

Here, I share with you what I have learned—insights that can help you unleash your potential as you navigate your way through a chaotic world.

 Roland Mees is a Professor of Practice of Business Ethics at the Faculty of Economics and Business at the University of Groningen. Before entering academia, he was Director of Sustainable Finance at ING Wholesale Banking until mid-2025, where he worked closely with CFOs, treasurers, and sustainability managers of major global companies. He is the inventor of the Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL), a financial product that links loan interest rates to a company’s year-on-year sustainability performance, measured through independently verified Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
Alongside his role at ING, he completed a PhD at the Ethics Institute of Utrecht University in 2017, with his research monograph published in 2020. His work explores why it is so difficult to motivate action toward preserving the planet for future generations. At the RUG, he inspires students by showing how personal growth can develop along parallel paths that eventually converge to create positive change. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Before You Use AI, Regulate Your Brain | Leo van Woerden | TEDxUniversityofGroningen
recentItems.description:
Artificial intelligence doesn't just process data — it amplifies whatever mental state you bring to it, turning your noise into professional-looking nonsense.

When you work with your brain's natural rhythms, you unlock the creativity, critical thinking and intuition that AI can amplify but not guide.

The real difference in the age of AI isn't more software — it's a well-regulated human mind doing the leading. Leo van Woerden is a neuroscientist, sleep expert, and speaker with more than 25 years of research experience on the brain, stress, performance, and recovery. His work focuses on a defining challenge of our time: as technology becomes more powerful, how do people remain clear, adaptive, and resilient under increasing pressure?
In his TEDx talk, Leo explores why the real bottleneck is often not the technology itself, but the human system trying to keep up with it. This directly connects to the theme of growth. Real growth does not begin with more speed, more output, or more tools, but with the capacity to recover, regulate, and make sound decisions in complex environments. His message is clear: sustainable growth depends on how well we understand and train the brain and body that must navigate change. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: People power | Tony Myers | TEDxButterfish Cove
recentItems.description: Tony Myers is a sustainability professional dedicated to advocating for the power of green careers and working to inspire the next generation to enter the sustainability workforce. Green building initiatives have grown consistently since he joined the field in 2013. Better tech and tighter Building Energy Performance Standards exist, yet the talent pipeline remains thin. Technology gives us the tools, but skilled people give us our future. Tony Myers is a sustainability professional bridging the "Green Skills" gap. Since 2020, he has managed the State of Maryland’s Department of General Services Energy Audit Program, leading eco-initiatives across public facilities. Tony began his energy efficiency career in 2013, progressing from refrigeration upgrades to large commercial retrofits. In 2022, he joined MoCo Green Futures to fight the environmental talent shortage. Through this role, he champions green careers and inspires the next generation to enter the workforce. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What if your pain has a purpose? | Dr. Sunita Punjabi, PhD | TEDxButterfish Cove
recentItems.description: In this powerful talk, Dr. Sunita Punjabi reveals how the stories we tell ourselves shape our identity, beliefs, and future. Blending neuroscience with personal insight, she shows how we can rewrite those stories and turn adversity into transformation. Dr. Sunita Punjabi, PhD is a neuropsychologist, licensed professional counselor, researcher, and founder of Brain Coach LLC. Her work focuses on neuroplasticity, human behavior, purpose-driven living, and brain optimization. As founder of the Texas Brain Science Symposium, she translates complex neuroscience into practical strategies that help individuals and organizations improve engagement, resilience, and performance. Through research, clinical practice, and speaking engagements, Dr. Punjabi empowers audiences to unlock human potential and create lasting transformation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Farm to Table | Matthew Kern | TEDxButterfish Cove
recentItems.description: Matthew Kern reflects on his career journey as a chef, from starting as a dishwasher to discovering a passion for fine dining, sustainability, and farm-to-table cooking. Inspired by local farmers and the importance of reducing food waste, he shares how using ingredients thoughtfully can reconnect us to our communities and the stories behind what we eat. Through his philosophy to “leave room for life to happen,” Matthew encourages us to embrace simplicity, find purpose in what we do, and discover peace in learning to live with less. Raised in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, Matt grew up surrounded by food- from homemade pasta, to big family dinners, his passion for food started at an early age and eventually led to his first restaurant job at age 14. Having spent the last 16 years in Coastal Delaware, he has been One Coastal’s Executive Chef and Owner for the past 5 years, leading our kitchen with passion, and a true love of what he is doing. Through his extensive connections with local farmers, Matt is able to gather and produce beautiful food for One Coastal, that is hyper-seasonal and locally sourced. From oysters to soft shells, Chef is thrilled by unique ingredients that allow him to tell a humble story. Matt was Delaware’s first ever Finalist for “Best Chef Mid-Atlantic “ for the James Beard Foundation, and a semifinalist in 2019-2020. When not at the restaurant, Chef usually spends his time hanging out with his adorable Wife & Children, or fly fishing some secret Delaware “Honey Hole” for local fish. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The loneliness of success | Dr. Krishna Athal | TEDxButterfish Cove
recentItems.description: Why do the people who seem to have everything so often feel the most unseen? Drawing on neuroscience, psychology, and more than a decade of coaching senior leaders, Dr Krishna Athal reveals the five traits that quietly turn extraordinary success into extraordinary isolation, and names “the applause gap”: the distance between how celebrated you are and how known you feel. He closes with three small steps, Audit, Anchor, Allow, for finding your way back to being truly known. Dr Krishna Athal is a scholar-practitioner who works at the intersection of leadership, psychology, neuroscience, and human behavior. He is a life and executive coach, corporate trainer, and leadership consultant who has spent years studying how influence actually operates in real systems, not just in theory, but in boardrooms, teams, institutions, and everyday relationships. His work focuses on sustainable behavioral change, emotional resilience, and practical leadership maturity, helping individuals and organizations move from performance to presence, from control to clarity, and from charisma to clean influence. Known for blending sharp social observation with grounded compassion, he teaches leadership as a posture practice: when to step forward, when to step back, and how to build cultures where truth, dignity, and accountability can survive daylight. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The past and future of EV charging | Nick McNulty | TEDxButterfish Cove
recentItems.description: Join Nick McNulty as he discusses the expansion of the EV Charging industry in the United States through his personal lens over the last 15 years. Learn more about the math behind charging times, how much EV infrastructure has grown in the US recently, and some of the exciting EV news on the horizon. Nick McNulty is the Managing Director of Blue Whale EV, where he leads the development and deployment of electric vehicle charging infrastructure projects. With a background in client success, business development, and project management, he has helped municipalities, schools, commercial property owners, and multifamily communities implement EV charging solutions. Nick is passionate about building strategic partnerships that expand access to EV charging. His interest in electrification began at Clarkson University, where he researched EV charging feasibility. Outside of work, he enjoys kayaking on the Chesapeake Bay and exploring national parks. recentItems.title: Who said birthdays need cake? | Max Stéfani | TEDxEscola Concept Ribeirão Preto
recentItems.description:
In this TEDx presentation, Max de Stéfani reflects on the dangers of social conformity and the importance of embracing individuality. The speaker shares his experience of celebrating his birthday by exploring Itatiaia National Park with friends, swapping a traditional party for mountain trails and outdoor games,to question why we so often choose to go with the flow and do only what is expected. He references Solomon Asch's famous conformity experiment to demonstrate how group pressure leads people to ignore their own perceptions just to fit in.
Max warns that constantly trying to align with social trends and others' expectations can distance us from who we truly are and stifle creativity. He invites the audience to view authenticity not as something to hide, but to celebrate, reminding us that the most meaningful experiences and world-changing ideas come from challenging expectations rather than following them.
 Grade 7 student at Escola Concept Ribeirão Preto This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Woman Beyond the Horizon | Fatima Bukar Lamisula | TEDxMaiduguri
recentItems.description:
In this deeply personal and powerfully reflective talk, Hon. Fatima Lamisula invites the audience to rethink what a “horizon” truly is. Drawing from her own journey, she reveals how the most challenging horizons are not the distant mountains or faraway dreams we imagine, but the invisible beliefs that quietly limit who we think we’re allowed to become.

With honesty and grace, she shares how she once confused sacrifice with disappearance—celebrating everyone else’s growth while neglecting her own. A turning point came when she realized she was grieving the woman she still had the potential to become. That awakening led her to confront the internal stories that had shaped her life and to step boldly into public service.

Through vivid storytelling, she highlights how countless people—women, young leaders, entire communities—live beneath these unseen boundaries. She argues that before systems fail, stories fail, and that leadership begins the moment someone refuses to believe a limiting narrative.

Hon. Fatima challenges us to consider the horizons we pass on to the next generation. Will we widen a child’s sense of possibility, or quietly teach her to shrink it?

Ultimately, she offers a powerful invitation: to question the invisible horizons of fear, tradition, grief, or self‑doubt, and to walk toward them with courage. Because beyond those horizons is not a different life—it is a fuller version of the life already waiting for us.

A talk for anyone standing at the edge of their own story, The Woman Beyond the Horizon reminds us that the horizon is not an ending, but the place where our next beginning waits. Hon. Fatima Lamisula is a Nigerian public servant, politician, policy influencer, entrepreneur, humanitarian, and orator passionate about shaping inclusive governance and empowering the next
generation of leaders. She serves as a Member of the Nigerian Youth Parliament and chairs its Committee on Women Affairs and Gender Equality, where she champions legislation and policy
reforms that advance youth participation, women’s political inclusion, and gender equality. She is a Member of the Open Government Partnership (OGP), contributing to initiatives that
promote transparency, accountability, citizen participation, and democratic governance. As the
Regional Director of Young United World Leaders (YUWL), she mentors emerging leaders and
drives initiatives that inspire civic engagement and transformational leadership across the region.
An accomplished entrepreneur, Fatima is the founder of In and Out Design, an event planning and creative solutions company, and ThreadMinds, a technology startup leveraging artificial intelligence and digital innovation to transform African industries while preserving cultural heritage and creating globally scalable opportunities.
With leadership experience spanning public policy, legislative advocacy, governance, and community development, Fatima has established herself as a respected voice on youth development,
women ’s leadership, democratic participation, and inclusive governance. She is committed to building stronger institutions, expanding opportunities for women and young people, and advancing innovative solutions that drive sustainable development and lasting social impact across Africa. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.description: 2015년 겨울, 텅 빈 용산 전자상가 지하 주차장에서 아이템도 없이 시작한 첫 창업. 허제는 하드웨어 액셀러레이터 N15를 공동 창업해 10년간 빠르게 키웠지만, 그 뒤에는 함께한 사람들과 방향이 갈라지는 갈등과 결국 회사를 떠나 다시 혼자가 된 방황의 시간이 있었다. 화려한 결과 뒤에 가려진 실패와 다시 걷기 시작한 이야기를 꺼내며, 그는 우리가 스스로 끝이라고 정하기 전까지는 아무것도 끝난 게 아니라고 말한다.  스털링어드바이저리 대표이자 스털링캐피탈파트너스 Managing Director. 드레이퍼 스타트업하우스 코리아 파트너, 싱가포르 ALXZA Holdings 벤처파트너로 활동하고 있다. 삼일PwC를 거쳐 하드웨어 특화 액셀러레이터 N15를 창업해 대표를 지냈다. recentItems.title: Our Education is Hard  | Dr. Mohammed Malah | TEDxMaiduguri
recentItems.description:
This talk challenges the current educational system in Nigeria as unnecessarily hard. He argues that hardship is not a prerequisite for success. He shared the story of his upbringing in Maiduguri, chronicling the story of Borno as a story of hardship but he asks a question, can a city be defined by its period of hardship despite all the years of prosperity. Juxtaposing this story with that of young people, he challenges people to see beyond the hardship regardless.  Dr Mohammed Malah is a chartered geoscientist and energy and climatepolicy professional with the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Sector. His career spans upstream petroleum regulation, emissions reduction, sustainability, carbon management, and climate policy.
His journey began in Maiduguri, where he attended Namu Primary
School, Federal Government College Maiduguri, and the University of
Maiduguri. He later obtained a master’s degree and PhD in Petroleum
Geoscience from the University of Manchester in the United Kingdom.
He also holds an MBA, which complements his technical background
with knowledge of strategy, leadership, and organisational management.
Over the years, he has contributed to policy development, regulatory
initiatives, research, professional dialogue, and capacity-building
programmes in Nigeria and across Africa. He is also committed to
mentoring young people and expanding access to knowledge and
opportunity. He considers himself a lifelong learner and continues to
broaden his knowledge across science, policy, leadership, and
management.
His work focuses on energy policy, sustainability, carbon management, and the transition to cleaner energy systems in Nigeria and across Africa. Beyond his professional work, he is interested in how communities can turn constraints into innovation, resilience, and new possibilities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
